prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1360; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reports being struck while the insured was turning left at an intersection. Claimant states they were a passenger in the vehicle and that the impact occurred on the driver's side.

Entry 2: Police attendance records confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene. No photographs, independent witness statements, or secondary reports of the collision have been located to date.

Entry 3: Insured is listed as the driver on the policy and confirmed the coverage in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection shows the damage is mostly consistent with the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle has been identified in our records or in the inspection notes.

Entry 5: Claimant reports neck and lower back pain and was seen at a medical facility the same week. The injury, a back strain, fits the type and force of a side impact of this kind.

Entry 6: Medical records show no earlier complaints or treatment to the same body area. Care followed a typical course and eased as the claimant improved over the following weeks.

Entry 7: Claimant has given the same account of the incident in each call and written statement so far. File review is complete pending final medical updates, and no further action is needed at this time.
